docs.title: BucketFlow
docs.text:
BucketFlow is a modern self-hosted file manager for S3-compatible storage.

It provides a single web interface to connect multiple providers, control user access, manage files and folders, and publish scoped public links.

Supported providers include AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, and other S3-compatible APIs.

docs.title: What BucketFlow provides
docs.text: Capability Description Multiple S3 destinations Connect and operate several storage backends at once Role-based access Admin and Editor roles with per-destination permissions Public links Create anonymous links scoped to a bucket or folder Link layouts Compact embed (iframe) or branded shared page Link permissions Read-only by default, optionally allow uploads, text-file editing, or folder creation File operations Browse, upload, download, ZIP, bulk delete, rename, preview and copy text, edit and save text files Bucket tools Create, rename, delete (admin) S3 metadata Custom user metadata; admins also see read-only object system metadata Embeddable viewer Embed the public view via iframe

docs.title: Embeddable Viewer
docs.text: BucketFlow public view can be embedded into any website via iframe.

docs.title: Basic example
docs.text:
<iframe
  src="https://your-domain.com/public?path=your-public-link-hash"
  width="100%"
  height="600"
  frameborder="0"
></iframe>

docs.title: Theme parameters
docs.text:
You can pass theme settings through query parameters:

?path=your-public-link-hash&primary=emerald&neutral=zinc&theme=dark
  • path — public link hash
  • primary — primary color
  • neutral — neutral palette
  • theme — system (default), light, or dark
  • omit view=page in embed URLs so the compact layout without a header is used (the generated iframe code always does this)

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• create separate links for specific folders/use cases;
  • use read-only links for public embedding by default;
  • enable upload/folder creation only when required.

docs.title: File Manager
docs.text: After login, the main file manager is displayed.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• S3 Destination — select active destination
  • Refresh buckets — reload buckets for the selected destination
  • Bucket sidebar — switch between buckets; drag the right edge to resize (width is remembered)
  • Bucket size — admins see used storage next to each bucket name
  • Breadcrumbs — navigate nested folders
  • Grid/List — toggle layout mode
  • List sorting — sort by name, size, or date; dates use DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm format

Row actions (metadata, rename, download, preview, delete) appear as icons on each file or folder in both views.

docs.title: Available operations
docs.text: Operation Description Browse Explore files and folders in current bucket Upload Upload one or multiple files Download Download a single file Download selected Bulk download selected files/folders as ZIP Delete selected Bulk delete selected files/folders after confirmation Preview Preview images, PDF, and text files; copy text; editors can edit and save text files Create folder Create a folder in the current path Rename file/folder Rename file or folder Delete file/folder Delete a single file or folder Metadata View/edit S3 object metadata

docs.title: Text-file preview and editing
docs.text:
The preview supports common text and source-code formats, including .txt, .md, .json, .js, .ts, .html, .css, .yaml, .py, and .sql. Text files are recognized by their file extension.

  • Select Copy in the preview to copy the displayed text. While editing, it copies the current draft.
  • Editors can select Edit, then Save to store their changes or Cancel to discard them. The preview is read-only until editing is started.
  • In a public link, text editing is available only when Allow text file edit is enabled. It applies only to existing text files inside the link's shared path; it does not allow uploads.

docs.title: Folder names
docs.text:
A folder name is a single path segment:

  • 1–255 characters after trim
  • no / or \
  • not . or ..

Create nested folders by opening a parent folder first, then creating a new folder there.

docs.title: Bulk actions
docs.text:
• Select multiple rows (list) or tiles (grid)
  • Download — one file downloads directly; multiple items or folders become a ZIP
  • Delete — confirmation lists how many files and folders will be removed; this cannot be undone

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
If destination Metadata columns are configured, those keys appear as table columns.

  • User-defined metadata — key-value pairs stored with the object; editors can change them
  • Object metadata (admin only) — read-only system fields from S3 HeadObject (content type, size, ETag, last modified, and related headers)

docs.title: Bucket operations (admin only)
docs.text:
These actions sit on the main toolbar, not in the sidebar.

  • Create New Bucket — create a bucket
  • Rename Bucket — rename the selected bucket
  • Delete Bucket — empty and delete the selected bucket, then remove public links that targeted it. You must type the bucket name to confirm. This cannot be undone.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Method Requirements Docker Docker 20.10+ and Docker Compose v2 Local Node.js 20+, pnpm 10+

docs.title: Option A: run from repository source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ambyte/bucketflow.git
cd bucketflow
docker compose up -d

This option uses the local Dockerfile and is ideal for development or custom builds.

docs.title: Option B: pre-built GHCR image
docs.text:
Create a docker-compose.yml with the following service:

services:
  bucketflow:
    image: ghcr.io/ambyte/bucketflow:latest
    container_name: bucketflow
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - bucketflow-data:/app/.data/storage
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://localhost:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

volumes:
  bucketflow-data:

Then run:

docker compose up -d

docs.title: Docker setup benefits
docs.text:
• Automatic restart (restart: unless-stopped)
  • Persistent data storage in bucketflow-data (users, destinations, generated JWT/encryption keys)
  • Health checks on /api/health

docs.title: First launch
docs.text:
1. Open http://localhost:3000
  2. On first run, create the initial admin account
  1. Go to Admin Panel → S3 Configuration and add your first destination

Field details are documented in S3 Destinations.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ambyte/bucketflow.git
cd bucketflow
pnpm install
pnpm dev

The app will be available at http://localhost:3000.

Build and preview production locally:

pnpm build
pnpm preview

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
On first start the server generates a JWT signing secret and an encryption key and stores them with application data (the Docker volume path above). Keep that volume.

Other defaults:

  • Session JWT is an HttpOnly bf-auth cookie (24 hours), not localStorage
  • Login is limited to 10 attempts per IP per 15 minutes; first-admin registration to 5 per IP per 15 minutes
  • Destination secret keys are encrypted at rest
  • App routes send a Content-Security-Policy; /public allows iframe embedding

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution Port 3000 is already in use Change port mapping, e.g. "8080:3000" Container exits immediately Check logs: docker compose logs bucketflow Data seems missing after restart Ensure bucketflow-data is used and avoid docker compose down -v unless intentional Health check fails initially Wait 10–30 seconds after startup, especially on first boot

docs.text:

docs.title: Technologies
docs.text:
• Nuxt 4
  • Nuxt UI
  • AWS SDK v3 for S3 API access
  • JWT in an HttpOnly cookie + bcryptjs for authentication
  • Zod for API input validation

docs.title: S3 compatibility
docs.text: BucketFlow supports any S3-compatible endpoint with proper endpoint, region, and forcePathStyle configuration when needed.

docs.title: Public Sharing
docs.text: Public links are available only for destinations with Allowed anonymous access enabled.

docs.title: Creating a public link
docs.text:
1. Select a destination with public access enabled
  2. Open target bucket/folder
  3. Click Public Link
  4. Copy URL or iframe embed code

docs.title: Link settings
docs.text:
• target bucket/path;
  • expiration date (or permanent link);
  • layout: Embed (no header, for iframe) or Shared page (BucketFlow header, shared path, color-mode button);
  • public page theme (primary, neutral, theme); iframe copies always use embed layout;
  • permissions:
  • Allow file upload — allow uploading new files;
  • Allow text file edit — allow editing existing supported text files in the shared path. This permission is independent of file upload;
  • Allow folder creation — allow creating folders.

docs.title: Public URL format
docs.text:
https://your-domain.com/public?path=<hash>&primary=emerald&neutral=zinc&theme=system
https://your-domain.com/public?path=<hash>&view=page&primary=emerald&neutral=zinc&theme=system
Parameter Description path Public link hash (required) view page for a branded share page with header; omit or embed for iframe primary Primary theme color neutral Neutral palette theme system (default), light, or dark

docs.title: Managing existing links
docs.text:
In Manage Public Links you can:

  • list destination links;
  • open the public page;
  • copy URL;
  • edit settings (including expiration and permissions);
  • delete links.

docs.title: Security behavior
docs.text:
• access is scoped to link bucket/path;
  • admin features are unavailable in public mode;
  • default mode is read-only unless upload, text-file editing, or folder creation is explicitly enabled;
  • public text-file editing only applies to existing supported text files within the shared path and does not enable file uploads;
  • text editing is disabled by default and can be changed when creating or editing a link.

docs.title: S3 Destinations
docs.text:
An S3 destination is a connection to a specific S3-compatible provider.

Configuration is available in Admin Panel → S3 Configuration.

docs.title: Adding a destination
docs.text:
1. Open Admin Panel → S3 Configuration
  2. Click Add Destination
  3. Fill in the fields
Field Purpose Name Display name of the destination Access Key ID S3 access key Secret Access Key S3 secret key. Required when creating. When editing, leave blank to keep the stored key (the secret is never shown again) Buckets Optional space-separated bucket allow-list Metadata columns Space-separated metadata keys displayed as file table columns Region Provider region, e.g. us-east-1 Endpoint S3 endpoint URL, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com Force Path Style Enable for MinIO and similar services Allowed Users Editors allowed to access this destination Allowed anonymous access Enables public links and anonymous access

Secrets are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) in the app data store. The API never returns the secret to the browser.

docs.title: Additional actions
docs.text:
• Test Connection — validate connectivity before saving
  • Edit — update destination settings (omit the secret to keep the current one)
  • Delete — remove destination (does not delete data from S3)

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text:
• AWS S3
  • Cloudflare R2
  • MinIO
  • Wasabi
  • DigitalOcean Spaces
  • Any S3-compatible API

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
This section is available at Admin Panel → Users.

Only Editor users are created via UI. The first admin account is created on initial setup.

docs.title: Creating an editor user
docs.text:
1. Open Admin Panel → Users
  2. Click Add User
  3. Enter username (minimum 3 characters)
  4. Enter password (minimum 6 characters) and confirmation
  5. Click Create User

docs.title: Editing and deleting users
docs.text:
• Edit — update username and/or password
  • Delete — remove an editor user
  • Current admin has a dedicated Change credentials flow

After creating editor users, grant destination access in S3 Destinations using Allowed Users.

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text: BucketFlow uses two roles: Admin and Editor.

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
Admin has full access to:

  • all destinations and buckets;
  • the Admin Panel;
  • creating/updating/deleting S3 destinations;
  • user management;
  • bucket creation, rename, and delete;
  • bucket used-size in the sidebar;
  • all file operations, including bulk delete;
  • read-only S3 object (system) metadata in the metadata dialog;
  • enabling public access on destinations.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
Editor can work only with destinations assigned by an admin:

  • browse, upload, download, bulk-delete, and rename files;
  • create, delete, and rename folders;
  • edit user-defined object metadata;
  • work with public links only on destinations that allow anonymous access.

Editor limitations:

  • no Admin Panel access;
  • no user management;
  • no bucket creation, rename, or delete;
  • no bucket size listing;
  • no S3 system (object) metadata panel.
